videos.desc: A young woman in a pink and mint traditional Korean dress spins in front of a tiled palace gate in daylight. She then sits at a night street-food market strung with paper lanterns, eating an orange rice cake from a paper cup and pulling a wide-eyed face at the taste. The last shot is a night city crossing where whole building fronts are covered in glowing electric signs in red, blue and yellow; a bus passes behind her while she makes a small finger heart.

Dusk on a road beside a bare-treed park. A woman in a red beret, a knitted scarf and a fur-hooded parka holds the camera at arm's length and pulls it along behind her, glancing back and laughing. Above and behind her an ornate cast-iron lamp on a tall post burns orange against the deep blue evening sky, and a line of the same lamps recedes along the road, their light pooling on the tarmac and the pavement. She leads on into a wide open square where strings of white lights hang overhead and more lit lamps stand along the edges.

A young woman in a leopard-print coat stands at the edge of a very wide city street, one arm raised to hail a cab. The camera looks straight down the avenue: several lanes wide, lined with tall buildings on both sides and packed with yellow taxis stretching to the horizon. She pulls a wheeled suitcase, turns to the camera grinning, then holds her arm out over the crosswalk again as taxis roll past her.

Phone footage of a guided tour through an ancient Greek hilltop site. The camera moves up a stone ramp between rows of huge fluted marble pillars that carry the roof of a ruined gateway, following a guide who holds a red umbrella up above the group. The tour walks out into an open ruined courtyard where tourists stop and photograph the walls, then the clip cuts to a viewpoint at sunset where a large crowd on a paved terrace looks across the city at the temple standing on its rock.

Phone footage from inside a car stuck in morning traffic. A schoolboy in a white shirt and dark tie sits by the open window with cars packed around him and leans out to look along the jammed lanes as scooters squeeze past. He then walks up the steps of a pedestrian footbridge and takes hold of its metal railing with both hands, standing at the horizontal bar between its upright supports and looking down at hundreds of cars filling every lane of the hazy motorway below.

A travel reel in three parts. First a young woman in a white embroidered shirt leads the camera by the hand through a field of sunflowers at sunset. Then she walks across a cobbled cathedral square as a flock of pigeons takes off around her in front of a white church with golden domes. Finally the clip ends in the paved courtyard of an old manor: the walls and arcades of the building close the space in on every side, strings of warm lights hang overhead, and a long table of guests in embroidered shirts claps and cheers as she lifts a big braided loaf of bread above her head.

A young man in a red jacket with a backpack turns on the spot in the middle of a busy city crossing, arms flung wide and mouth open in delight. All around and above him the building fronts are covered floor to roof in enormous lit advertising boards - bright pink, blue and white panels the size of whole walls, stacked one above the other and wrapped around the corners of the towers - while yellow taxis and crowds pass behind him. The clip then cuts to him leaning on the rail of a ferry, grinning, with a tall green statue on an island behind him, and finally to him standing on a rock at the rim of a huge red canyon at sunset with his arms raised.

A montage of people walking. First a low shot follows a woman in a navy business suit and nude high heels striding along a city sidewalk past taxis and office workers; then she is seen from behind crossing a street between glass skyscrapers in the financial district. The scene cuts to a bald hiker with a big backpack and trekking poles climbing a forest trail towards a mountain; then to a man in a blue t-shirt walking a golden retriever on a leash across a sunny park lawn; and finally to a high aerial view of a huge crowd streaming across the Shibuya-style crossing between illuminated billboards downtown.

A modern red-brick apartment building with rows of balconies glows in low golden sun. A young woman in a white vest top and grey jeans pulls a big green velvet sofa up on a rope over the railing of her balcony until it lands inside, then cheers with a raised fist. Neighbours on the other balconies watch, two older women wave their arms and men lean over the railings. Washing and potted plants hang on the balconies and a van stands in the street below.

In a crowded city park on a hot sunny day, a young man in an olive polo shirt and shorts crouches on the grass and turns a metal key in a sprinkler valve in the ground, sending a strong jet of water sideways with a small rainbow in it. Behind him the picnic crowd scatters in every direction: two young women run holding a blanket over their heads, a man leaps over a hedge and runs past, and a dog runs along. More sprinklers spray near a gazebo, and the young man looks calmly up.

In a narrow second-hand bookshop on a rainy day, a young man with wet hair, a dark wool coat speckled with raindrops and a brown scarf leans lazily against a tall bookshelf with his hands in his pockets, glancing up at the book spines. He straightens, points idly at a shelf without taking any book, then leans back against the shelf again. Shelves packed with books line both sides, boxes of books sit on the wooden floor, and a young woman writes at a desk by the rainy window.

A small empty cafe in soft daylight has round marble tables with black iron bases and curved wooden chairs in front of a grey counter with a marble top. On the counter stand a glass case full of croissants and pastries, a steaming espresso machine, stacks of cups and a coffee grinder, under copper pendant lamps. Water flows in through the open glass door and spreads over the patterned tiled floor around a single cup and saucer, and the street outside is flooded too.

In a narrow cobbled street in a sunny old village, a laughing young woman in a white blouse, olive trousers and sandals pulls hard on a long white rope that runs up to a pulley on a wall, hoisting a wicker basket towards a balcony. The basket holds a small scruffy dog, a baguette and flowers. It rises to the balcony, where a woman reaches for it, and the woman below lets go and laughs. Coils of rope lie on the stones and an old man sits on a chair nearby.

On a sunny stone square in an old town, a black cloth comes off a life-size statue of clear ice standing on a stone plinth, and a broken ice hand lies in a puddle on the ground. A young man in a flat cap, white shirt and black waistcoat holds the black cloth and grins beside the shiny, dripping ice figure. The ice melts in the hot sun and water runs down onto the plinth. Tourists in summer clothes watch, and cafe tables stand under tall shuttered buildings.

Brown floodwater covers a street of tall stone tenement buildings and fills the ground-level flats. A young woman in a yellow jacket sits in a wooden rowing boat right outside an open front door and paddles away from the building, the water swirling behind the boat. Tables and chairs are piled up inside the flooded room beside her, and a sofa and sandbags stand in the water outside. Above, a neighbour leans out of a dry upper window. A bicycle stands in the water.

On an evening in a stone square lit by old street lamps under a pink sky, a public meeting fills curved stone steps with dozens of people of all ages, some raising their hands. In the middle a young woman in a mustard shirt talks into a microphone and points towards the crowd, then turns and keeps speaking. A white architectural model of buildings and trees stands on a table beside her. A man in a suit and another in a grey shirt sit on chairs listening, and the man in the suit gestures.

On a hillside neighbourhood in warm afternoon sun, hundreds of small brick and concrete houses, some painted green, yellow, blue and pink, are packed closely together up the steep slope, with flat roofs, water tanks, satellite dishes and tangled wires between them. In the foreground a young woman in a pink vest top, a patterned skirt and a headscarf walks up worn concrete steps between the houses, away from the viewer, carrying a basket of laundry on her hip, and gets smaller as she climbs.

In a sunny city park, a big red, yellow and blue hot air balloon crash-lands behind a wooden bench, its wicker basket tearing up the grass while the pilot clings on, and people run and a dog dashes away. On the bench a young woman with long black hair, headphones and sunglasses on her head, in a white shirt and beige trousers, calmly reads a book and sips an iced drink through a straw, a paper bag of pastries beside her. She never looks up while the basket tips over and families picnic further back.

A narrow old-town street on a sunny festival day, with yellow houses, washing lines and coloured bunting. A smiling young man in a white shirt leans over a balcony railing and slowly lets down a wicker basket on a rope, with a fluffy ginger cat sitting inside it. On the cobbles below, a baker in a white apron reaches up with a long loaf of bread towards the basket. A brass band in white shirts plays in a big crowd under falling confetti, and neighbours look out of other windows.

An abandoned funfair at dusk. An old merry-go-round lit up with hundreds of warm bulbs turns in a haze of mist, its painted wooden horses going round, although weeds and long grass grow all around it. A fox stands in the grass and watches, and the lights reflect in a rippled puddle on the cracked concrete. Behind it stand a broken ticket booth covered in ivy and a big Ferris wheel under a cloudy blue evening sky.

A sunny cobbled street with striped café awnings and white bunting overhead. A young woman in a blue blazer, white blouse and black trousers, holding a brown handbag, stops in the middle of the street and dances right there, spinning and stepping, laughing. Beside her two young street dancers in bright shell suits with a portable speaker on the ground cheer her on, and behind her a young woman in a lilac suit and other people watch and clap, some with raised hands.

A sunny city street. A young man in a navy suit, with his blue tie flying and a black briefcase under his arm, pulls hard on the handle of a glass office door and then pushes against the glass with his flat hand, but the building stays locked. Behind him the street is closed to traffic and full of people with the day off: a woman in a yellow top and red skirt dances, a man jumps to catch a frisbee, a cyclist rides past and friends sit on blankets under colourful bunting.

Inside a packed underground train, seen as a selfie. A grinning young woman in a red puffer jacket and a white beanie is squeezed against a young man in a blue coat. All around them people in winter coats stand pressed together, holding the poles and hand straps. A businessman in a suit holds his briefcase above his head to make space, and a woman holds her coffee cup high in the crowd. As the crowd pushes, the young woman's smile turns into a shocked face. Bright ceiling lights run along the carriage.

A sunny stone square with a church clock tower, a fountain and pigeons. A man painted all over in bronze, posing as a street statue on a wooden box, suddenly bends forward, takes off his bronze hat and holds it out to a young woman in a white shirt and blue skirt. She jumps back with her mouth wide open in shock, then laughs with her hands at her chest. Her friend in a pink T-shirt grabs her arm, and an older man in a sun hat stands beside the box with his hand near his pocket.
